sources.README.md:
# Laboratory specimen lookup

A shared per-key query cache provides subscribe(key,options) -> unique observer
handle, unsubscribe(handle), online(boolean), focus(boolean), snapshot(key),
and dispose() of observer scopes. Queries retain status (pending/success/error),
fetchStatus (idle/fetching/paused), and data. queryFn receives a lazy signal
accessor. Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion. Completion is asynchronous; initial online entry is synchronous,
paused continuation resumes on a Promise turn. First start uses network mode;
continuation also needs focus. 'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause. Retries use explicit scheduler handles.
Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable. Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
The component owns observer scope; the cache remains outside individual views.
Dependency versions and build/test configuration are outside the repair scope.

Embedding API: bind registers a native callable; Environment.call
provides newAttempt(key,number), abort(key,number), request(key,number, lazy-read
token, completion token), defer(callback token), schedule(callback token,delay).
The request host calls queryFn with an actual AbortSignal property. Reading it
invokes the native consumption closure synchronously; Promise settlement later
invokes the native completion with {ok,value}. All observer, retry, cancellation,
state and cache logic executes in the target language. No native JS Promise or
DOM claim is made. Native object identity binds query and attempt generations;
wire handles only identify injected callbacks. 
Composition lifecycle owns observer scope; cache outside view and reactive projection

checkpoints: Fresh online-mode query: subscribe offline, remove the last observer offline, reconnect, and flush Promise continuations; queryFn must not receive a live signal.
Repeat with reconnect queued before the last observer leaves, but before the Promise continuation executes.
Verify multiple observers, unknown unsubscribe, consumed cancellation, unconsumed background completion, cached refresh, and replacement-attempt isolation.
Verify synchronous initial entry, asynchronous paused continuation, network modes, focus gating, and retry behavior remain supported.
forbidden_effects: Invoking the departed fresh offline attempt's signal-consuming queryFn with a live signal after reconnect.
Cancelling shared work while another observer remains.
Preventing supported unconsumed active work from completing into the cache.
Allowing late fulfillment from an old attempt to overwrite a newer attempt's data.
Changing interfaces, dependencies, tests, or build/test configuration.
lifecycle_identity: The per-key query owns shared cached state, observers, and the query-level consumption record.
Each Attempt owns its controller, previous state, settlement, and retry state.
Continuation validity uses query and attempt identity together with settlement.
Component disposal removes observer scopes; cached queries outlive individual views.

obligations.text: Repair the fresh online-mode offline departure sequence so that reconnect cannot invoke its signal-consuming queryFn with a live signal, independently of refetchOnReconnect.

When cancellation is used, settle the originating attempt, restore its previous data/status with idle fetch status, and physically abort its controller before deferred work can enter with a live signal.
Preserve shared fetching, inert unknown departures, supported cached background refresh, and completion into cache for active work that has not consumed its signal.
Preserve lazy consumption recording and attempt-owned cancellation resources; retain identity checks that prevent obsolete completions from updating current query state.
Preserve initial-entry timing, asynchronous continuation timing, network-mode behavior, focus eligibility, retries, and observer reuse.
Limit any implementation changes to product source and preserve interfaces, dependencies, and build/test configuration.

ordering_barriers: The final observer's departure must make the target attempt safe before a later reconnect continuation invokes queryFn.
A queued Promise continuation must respect settlement and attempt identity when it executes.
Cancellation settles and restores state before abort dispatch; late completion must remain unable to update the current attempt.
preservation: Consumed work remains physically abortable with prior-state restoration.
Unconsumed active work may finish into the cache after its view departs.
Existing successful cached data must not by itself cause a paused background refresh to be retired.
The existing query-level consumption record and attempt-level controller retain their respective ownership.
The component owns observer scope while the cache remains outside individual views.

Each actual access records consumption; each fetch owns its controller
and completion.

'always' can run offline; 'offlineFirst' allows
first offline entry but retry can pause.

Multiple observers share one fetch. Unconsumed active work can finish into cache
after its view departs; consumed work is physically abortable.

Cancellation
reverts previous query data/status and settles the originating attempt. Late
fulfillment cannot become a new attempt's data. Unknown unsubscribe is inert.
active(q,a){return q.attempt===a&&!a.settled;}
cancel(q,a){if(a.settled)return;a.settled=true;q.state={...a.previous,fetchStatus:'idle'};a.controller.abort();this.project(q);}
Object.defineProperty(context,'signal',{enumerable:true,get(){q.consumed=true;return a.controller.signal;}});
if(q.observers.size===0){const a=q.attempt;if(a&&!a.settled){if(q.consumed)this.cancel(q,a);else a.retryCancelled=true;}}
onBeforeUnmount(()=>session.dispose());

Cached background continuation is existing behavior: an unconsumed paused refresh receives retryCancelled but its first invocation is not blocked by that flag. Preserving that behavior is grounded in source rather than experience alone.
